MRI LEFT KNEE

Clinical details: 24-year-old. Twisting injury playing football two weeks ago with immediate swelling. Positive Lachman's test.

Technique: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the left knee at 3T.

Comparison: No previous imaging available for comparison.

Findings:
Menisci: Vertical longitudinal tear of the peripheral third of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, with signal unequivocally reaching the articular surface on two consecutive images. The medial meniscus is intact. No displaced meniscal fragment.
Cruciate ligaments: Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, with no intact fibres traced from the femoral attachment. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.
Collateral ligaments: The medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex are intact. The posterolateral corner structures are intact. No Segond fracture.
Extensor mechanism: The extensor mechanism is unremarkable. Patellofemoral alignment is normal.
Articular cartilage: Articular cartilage is preserved in all three compartments.
Bone marrow: Bone marrow oedema at the lateral femoral condyle sulcus and posterolateral tibial plateau. No fracture.
Joint and soft tissues: Moderate joint effusion. No Baker's cyst. The surrounding soft tissues are unremarkable.

Impression:
1. Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear with associated bone bruising.
2. Peripheral vertical longitudinal tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, potentially amenable to repair.
Suggest orthopaedic knee clinic review.
